subject: sociology
title: Theorists in Action
welcome_lead: From Durkheim's organic analogy to Goffman's stage, see how key thinkers apply their theory to real social life.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying functionalist, Marxist, feminist and interactionist thinkers to society.
final_note: Linking a thinker to a theory and a study is exactly what AO2 marks reward.

concepts.def: Durkheim: society is like a body with linked organs.
A system in which men hold most social power.
Goffman: life as a stage with front and back regions.
A grand story explaining society, e.g. Marxism.
Agreement on shared norms and values.

walkthroughs.body_html: Durkheim argued institutions like religion produce social solidarity. Parsons claimed the family performs primary socialisation and school performs secondary socialisation, sorting children for adult roles.
Marx said workers create surplus value the capitalists keep. Althusser added that schools, media and religion act as ideological state apparatuses that keep workers in false consciousness.

Radical feminist Germaine Greer argues patriarchy oppresses women through family and culture. Interactionist Erving Goffman shows how individuals 'perform' identity, presenting different selves at school, work or with friends.
